One element I see here is that modern women have been pressured to feel that every pregnancy is so rare and costly that for an infant to die is the worst possible thing that could happen. That is partly AMA-created.

I think that the embrace of abortion was the flip side of this--the psychological compensation.

If a woman is only able to have one or two kids, and she fears that either or both will be mutants who cannot possibly be allowed to die naturally, then that is going to fuck with her inborn drives to health and wholeness. 

That's the thing that never gets discussed with the rise of abortion. There was a lot of discussion in the '70s and '80s of abortion being a last resort for women who knew (via medical examination/testing) that they were carrying terrible mutants. Which, if brought to birth, would have to be preserved at all costs. Which means not only being enslaved to that process but turning one's mutant offspring over to the medical industrial complex for TORTURE.

This cannot produce healthy mothers or women. 

My grandmothers both had 30% more children than survived, and my maternal grandmother saw two of her kids die in their teens in industrial mishaps. 

But also, the high infant mortality rate of previous times also correlates to stupidity about hygiene. In my paternal line, from Eastern Finland, they birthed their babies in a tannin-soaked smoke sauna and everybody baked regularly themselves (artificial fevers as part of daily life). They had large families and few died.
